newsitem.title: USA: White House hopes for full budget bill.
newsitem.headline: White House hopes for full budget bill.

text.p: White House budget director Franklin Raines said Thursday the Clinton administration hopes Congress will produce a full bill to fund the federal government for fiscal 1997 before the fiscal year begins next Tuesday.
Raines said at a White House news briefing there was sufficient time to pass a spending bill for the whole year without resorting to an interim bill, known as a Continuing Resolution (CR).
"It is our hope that they will be able to get an omnibus bill done without the need for any interim CR," Raines said.

Congress is still working on bills appropriating funds for six areas of the federal government for fiscal 1997, and must either roll them into an omnibus bill or pass an interim measure to avoid a partial government shutdown next Tuesday.
"We see no reason why the Congress can't complete its work (by October 1)," Raines said, adding that the White House was ready to enter negotiations as soon as an omnibus bill was complete.
